verdict.rationale: Discord documents its own REST API for interacting with Discord data, with bot-token and OAuth2 authentication. It also documents a Gateway for server events such as channel updates and role creation, HTTP webhooks, and Social SDK APIs for relationships and DMs, so there is real programmatic coverage of core surfaces. Nothing in the pack shows that the API matches everything a user can do in the UI. Missing for 10: any documented claim of API parity with the UI, evidence covering user-level actions such as Nitro and profile customization or server settings, a published OpenAPI spec (the probe returned 404s), and independent hands-on corroboration of API breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: 1. Using a bot token... 2. Using an OAuth2 bearer token
The Gateway API lets apps open secure WebSocket connections with Discord to receive events about actions that take place in a server/guild, like when a channel is updated or a role is created.
Manage Discord user relationships including friends and blocked users in your application.
